7.2.2 Control of cracking without direct calculation (deemed-to-satisfy)}

T23

Clause 7.2.2 of the code suggests that if the deemed-to-satisfy rules in the code
with respect to minimum reinforcement areas and bar spacings are followed, then
usually no direct calculation needs to be carried out to check compliance with the
crack width limits. As an altermative to following the deemed-to-satisfy rules,
direct calculation may be carried out to check compliance with the crack width
limits. According to Clause 7.2.1 of the code, in most cases, direct calculation to
check compliance with the crack width limits would allow wider bar spacings to
be used, especially for shallow members.

Assessment of crack widths

Only the crack width under long-term condition needs to be assessed. The loads
to be applied should be those of the frequent load combination (for prestressed
members with bonded tendons) or the quasi-permanent load combination (for
reinforced members and prestressed members with unbonded tendons), while the
elastic modulus of the concrete should be the long-term modulus taken as one-
half of the short-term modulus.
